case.question: side effects steroid injection
case.expected_answer: Reported effects include increased localized pain, non-positional headaches resolving within 24 hours, facial flushing, anxiety and sleeplessness.
case.support_quote: Possible Side Effects of Lumbar Epidural Steroid Injection. In addition to risks from the injection, there are also potential side effects from the steroid medication itself. These tend to be rare and much less prevalent than the side effects from oral steroids.onetheless, reported side effects from epidural steroid injections include: 1  Localized increase in pain. 2  Non-positional headaches resolving within 24 hours. 3  Facial flushing. 4  Anxiety. 5  Sleeplessness.
case.source_qualification: Specifically lumbar epidural steroid injections in the source, not a universal list for every steroid injection. These five reported examples form the answer rubric, not a clinical recommendation.

passages.text: The most common side effect of steroid injections is known as a “flare.” This pain is felt for one or two days after the injection. It can be treated with ice and by resting the area injected. Other side effects might include: A rise in blood sugar level for diabetic patients for about five days.

Side-effects of local steroid injections can include a temporary flare-up of joint pain, infection, changes in your mood and thinning of the skin.ide-effects of local steroid injections can include a temporary flare-up of joint pain, infection, changes in your mood and thinning of the skin.

Some of the side effects that have been reported with steroid injections include the following: Cortisone flares can occur which involve pain that can be worse after the injection than before the shot. This usually improves within 12 to 48 hours. In dark-skinned patients, the area around the injection site can whiten.

Steroid injections can also cause muscle or tendon weakness, so you may be advised to rest the treated area for a few days after the injection. Other possible side effects can include infections, blushing, and thinning and lightening of the skin in the area where the injection is given.

If steroid use is brief (from a few days to a few weeks), it is possible that none of the listed side effects will occur. The side effects listed here generally do not occur when occasional steroid injections are given for arthritis, tendonitis, or bursitis.igns of inflammation include redness, warmth, swelling, and pain. Steroids reduce the production of chemicals that cause inflammation. This helps keep tissue damage as low as possible. Steroids also reduce the activity of the immune system by affecting the way white blood cells work.

reference.answer: Side effects of steroid injections include a temporary flare-up of joint pain, infection, changes in mood, thinning of the skin, and muscle or tendon weakness. Other effects may include a rise in blood sugar level for diabetic patients, whiteness around the injection site in dark-skinned patients, blushing, and whitening of the skin in the injected area.
